_about: What each friend says when they hang out with you (src/companion.js, loaded only then): hello and late (arriving), bye (going home), stories, facts (true ones) and sayings (told while you fish), walk (now and then on foot).

hello: Rods ready? Good. Me too.
There you are. The fish have been asking about you.
Right. Where are we fishing?
late: Sorry I took so long. Had to find my lucky hat.
Made it. Rowed the last bit with one oar.
bye: That is my time. I have to go. See you tomorrow.
Light's going, and so am I. Same time tomorrow?
My knees say home. See you tomorrow, friend.
stories: This reminds me of the time I hooked a cod so big it towed me round the point. I let it win. It earned it.
My father fished these rocks with a line and a bent nail. He caught more than I do with all this gear.
Once I sat here eight hours and caught one sardine. Best day of that whole year. Do not ask me why.
I lost a ring off this very rock. Twenty years later a gull dropped it on my boat. I am still not sure I believe it.
First fish I ever caught, I cried and put it back. Still do that with the small ones.
facts: A single cod can lay millions of eggs in one season. Not many make it, mind.
Most fish have no eyelids. They cannot blink at you, but they are watching.
sayings: A quiet line is not an empty line.
You do not catch the fish. You let it find you.
Bad days fishing still beat good days doing almost anything else.
walk: You walk fast for someone with nowhere to be.

hello: I am here. Let us be quiet together.
Ah. A good day for the water.
Hello, little friend. Lead the way.
late: Forgive me. The snow does not hurry, and neither do I.
Old legs, long road. But I came.
bye: The light is going. I must go home. See you tomorrow.
Enough for one day. Come find me tomorrow.
My fire will be cold. Tomorrow, then.
stories: When I was small, my grandmother cut a hole in the ice and we waited all day. She said waiting was the catch. I thought she was teasing.
One winter the ice sang all night, long low notes. In the morning a seal looked up at me through the hole, as if to ask if I heard it too.
I have fished through forty winters. Each one I thought, this is the last. Here I am.
I once followed a fox across the ice for an hour. It led me to the best fishing hole I ever found.
facts: The Arctic char lives farther north than any other freshwater fish.
A polar bear's skin is black under all that white fur.
sayings: The ice remembers what we forget.
Cold makes you honest. There is no time for anything else.
Patience is warm, if you wear it long enough.
walk: Slower. The ground tells you things.
You are kind to walk with an old woman.

hello: I brought bread. For the fish. Mostly.
Hello! Shall we sit by the water?
Oh good, I needed a walk.
late: Sorry, sorry. The ducks would not let me leave.
I am here! The pond needed one more look.
bye: I have to go and feed the pond. See you tomorrow!
That was lovely. Same again tomorrow?
The koi will miss me. Tomorrow, dear.
stories: I named my first koi Pebble. She lived longer than my first three teapots.
Once a heron stole a fish right out of my bucket and then stared at me like I owed it another.
When it rains on the pond, I stand under the willow and watch the rings. Hours, sometimes. Do not tell anyone.
A boy once asked me if fish get bored. I said only if you are boring around them.
facts: Koi were bred from ordinary carp, for their colours, in Japan.
Goldfish remember things for months. The three-second memory is a myth.
sayings: Feed the pond and the pond feeds you back.
Still water is busy underneath.
Be gentle with slow things.
walk: Careful, there is a frog somewhere about.
I do love a walk with someone.

hello: Ready to get wet? Kidding. Mostly.
Hi! I have so many fish facts saved up.
Let us go see something.
late: Sorry! My hair is still drying.
I came straight from a dive. You would not believe the eel.
bye: Air's low, I have to go up. See you tomorrow!
I have to log my dive. Tomorrow?
That was great. Same time tomorrow?
stories: On my first dive I forgot to breathe out and my ears popped like corks. Now I hum the whole way down.
There is a wreck out past the reef with a piano in it. Still has three keys that work. I checked.
An octopus once took my glove and would not give it back. I let it keep it. It looked happier with it.
I saw a whale shark once. It went by so slowly I had time to cry and stop crying.
facts: Seahorse dads carry the babies until they hatch.
An octopus has three hearts.
Red is the first colour to fade as you dive. Deep down, blood looks green.
sayings: Down there the light comes in sideways. So does everything good.
Breathe slow, look long.
The sea is mostly unexplored. So is most of anything.
walk: I am much faster in fins.
Everything up here is so dry.

hello: Ahoy. Where are we headed?
Wind's good. Let us go.
Hey you. Need a deckhand?
late: Sorry I am late. The tide had other plans.
Here! Tied up two boats on the way.
bye: Tide's turning. I have to get back. See you tomorrow.
My watch starts soon. Tomorrow, sailor.
Back to the harbour for me. Tomorrow?
stories: My first boat leaked so much I named her Teacup. She got me everywhere, slowly.
Once in a fog we followed the sound of a bell for an hour. It was a goat. We still laugh about it.
I sailed through a storm so bad the gulls were walking. Came out the other side to a rainbow. Typical.
A dolphin rode our bow wave for a whole afternoon once. I talked to it the entire time.
facts: A knot is one nautical mile an hour. Sailors used to count knots on a rope as it ran out.
A nautical mile is a bit longer than a land mile.
sayings: Harbours are for leaving, and for coming home to.
You cannot change the wind. You can change the sail.
Every good trip starts with leaving the rope behind.
walk: Feels odd when the ground does not move.

hello: Hello hello! I found a shell shaped like a boot.
Adventure time?
I packed snacks. Berries. It is always berries.
late: Sorry! I got lost. On an island. Again.
Made it! Only fell in the water once.
bye: Sun's going, I have to get back to my hut. See you tomorrow!
I have to check my coconuts. Tomorrow?
Bye for now! Tomorrow, same island.
stories: I came here for a day trip. My boat drifted off while I napped. That was three summers ago, and I have never been happier.
I built a hut out of driftwood. Then a better hut. The first hut is now a crab's house.
I once traded a song for a fishing hook with a sailor. Best song I ever made up.
I keep a list of every bird I see. I have no idea what most of them are called, so I name them.
facts: A coconut can float across an ocean and still sprout on the other side.
Sea turtles swim back to the beach where they hatched to lay their own eggs.
sayings: I came for a day. That was three summers ago.
Getting lost is just finding somewhere early.
You do not need much. You need a little, and a view.
walk: Ooh, what is that? Oh. A rock.

hello: Keep your voice down.
You called. I came. Lead on.
I see you. I see everything.
late: Took the long way. Someone might have been following.
Late. Had to lose a tail.
bye: I have watch. Time to go. Tomorrow.
Sun's down. Lookouts look out at night. Tomorrow.
Enough. Tomorrow, same signal.
stories: Spent a whole season up a mast. Came down and the ground felt like a lie.
Spotted a ship on the horizon once and shouted so loud the captain dropped his soup. It was a cloud.
Had a parrot once. Knew more swear words than the crew. Then he learned to say please. Ruined him.
Captain hid a chest on a beach. Drew the map himself. Nobody has found it. Not even the captain.
facts: The lookout's perch at the top of a mast is called the crow's nest.
Real pirates hardly ever buried treasure. They spent it.
sayings: Watch the horizon. Trouble always waves first.
The jungle listens.
Look twice. Speak once.

hello: Hey! Got water? Good.
Let us go find a view.
Ready when you are.
late: Sorry, a dust devil chased me half the way.
Made it. Red sand everywhere, as usual.
bye: Gotta get back before dark. See you tomorrow!
Canyon's calling me home. Tomorrow?
That was great. Same again tomorrow.
stories: I got stuck on a ledge once for a whole night. Best stars I ever saw. Would not recommend.
Found a fossil fish in the red rock, miles from any sea. Made me feel very small, in a nice way.
I guide people up the cliffs. Most get halfway, sit down, and say this is fine actually. They are right.
A lizard rode on my hat for a whole afternoon. I named him Captain.
facts: Red rock gets its colour from iron. Basically, rust.
Each layer in a cliff can hold thousands of years.
Deserts can freeze at night, even after a scorching day.
sayings: Red rock gets under your nails and into your heart.
The view is worth the climb, every time.
Drink before you're thirsty.

hello: Good day to you. Shall we?
Ah, a friend. Where to?
I am at your service.
late: My apologies. The ledger would not balance itself.
Forgive the delay. I locked the dock twice to be sure.
bye: The dock needs its keeper. I must go. Until tomorrow.
Time to lock up. See you tomorrow.
A good day. Tomorrow, friend.
stories: My grandfather kept this dock, and his father before him. I found their names carved under the third plank.
A merchant once paid his mooring fee in figs. I accepted. They were very good figs.
I watched a sandstorm swallow a boat once. When it cleared, the boat was fine and covered in sand like a cake.
The stones of the old tomb hum on hot days. Science says expansion. I say they are remembering.
facts: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building in the world for nearly four thousand years.
The ancient Egyptians made paper, and even boats, from the papyrus plant.
sayings: The stones are older than the sea, I think.
Write it down. Memory is a leaky boat.
Keep the small promises. The big ones get easier.
walk: A fine day for a walk.

hello: Hello! I swept the steps twice, so I am free.
Oh, I am so glad you called!
Let us go somewhere green.
late: Sorry, sorry, it rained and the steps needed me.
I am here! I ran the whole way.
bye: I have to sweep the temple steps. See you tomorrow!
The rain is coming in. Tomorrow?
Thank you for today. Tomorrow!
stories: I sweep the same hundred steps every day. Every day they are a little different. I think that is the point.
A monkey once stole my broom and swept a step with it. Badly. But it tried.
When the big rain comes, the temple sounds like a drum. I lie on the floor and listen.
I found a tiny frog sitting in the stone bell once. I rang it very, very gently.
facts: Rainforests cover a small part of the Earth but are home to over half its kinds of plants and animals.
A tarpon can gulp air from the surface, like a breath.
sayings: It rains, and the steps shine, and I sweep them again.
Small work, done kindly, is not small.
Let the day be the size it is.
walk: Mind the moss, it is slippery.
